notes: Parts from step 1 are unchanged; no part was added or dropped.
The tutorial covers many exercises, but both images show only the light-sensing circuit, so only that one is built.

Pin mapping from the Fritzing image: the Pi is drawn rotated 180°. Red goes to pin 1 (3V3.1) and green to pin 7 (GPIO4), both in the upper row. Black goes to pin 6 (GND.1) in the lower row. This matches the code LightSensor(4).

Breadboard: red goes to column 1, green to column 3 and black to column 5, all in row a. The LDR spans columns 1 and 3, as in the second image. The capacitor spans columns 3 and 5, with its positive (long) leg in column 3 on the same strip as an LDR leg, as the manual says. The circuit is 3V3 → LDR → GPIO4 node → capacitor → GND.
Exact rows for the component legs (row e for the LDR, row d for the capacitor) are chosen only to avoid two legs sharing a hole. Any hole in the same column strip is electrically the same.
For the male-to-female jumpers, port a is assumed to be the female end on the Pi header and port b the male end in the breadboard.
The capacitor is catalogue type capacitor-10uf with value=1uF, because no 1μF type exists.
